items.title: Letters Went Out to 4.1 Million Patients This Week — Expect the Scam Calls Too
items.summary: Letters are arriving this week for 4.1 million customers of AdaptHealth — the company that delivers home medical equipment like sleep apnea and oxygen machines. Thieves stole names, health details, and insurance information. Scammers buy lists like this fast, so expect calls offering to "help you claim free credit monitoring." If you get a letter, use only the phone number printed on it — never one a caller gives you. And glance over your insurance statements for care you never received.

items.title: Your scanner needs its disc back? NAPS2 is the free download at naps2.com that makes any scanner work on a fresh computer
items.summary: NAPS2 (short for "Not Another PDF Scanner 2") is completely free scanner software — download it at naps2.com, click Install, and it works with HP, Canon, Epson, and Brother scanners, saving scans straight to searchable PDFs. No manufacturer disc, no account, no ads.

items.title: That old Windows computer your kid outgrew? Google's free ChromeOS Flex gives it a second life as a fast, simple Chromebook
items.summary: Google offers ChromeOS Flex completely free at chromeos.google/products/chromeos-flex — download it to a USB stick, plug it into your old Windows computer, and it becomes a fast, safe Chromebook-style machine that starts up in seconds and updates itself automatically.

items.title: The Biggest Windows Security Update Ever Went Out Tuesday — Install It Tonight
items.summary: Microsoft just shipped its biggest security update ever — nearly 1,000 fixes in a single day, and two of the holes being patched were already under attack. If your computer hasn't updated since Tuesday, it's missing protection against bugs criminals are using right now. Updating takes a few minutes, then restart when it asks. Put it off and you're leaving the door unlocked. Do it tonight.

items.title: Chrome now updates every two weeks — check yours free in the Chrome menu under About Google Chrome
items.summary: Google switched Google Chrome to a two-week update schedule as of September 8, which means the security fixes arrive twice as often — open Chrome, click the three-dot menu in the top corner, choose Help > About Google Chrome, and it checks and updates itself for free in under a minute.

items.title: iOS 27 arrives Monday September 14 — the free iPhone update with the new Siri, here's how to get it
items.summary: Apple releases iOS 27 this Monday, September 14 — free for iPhone 11 and newer — with the redesigned Siri that can follow up on questions and a battery-friendly overhaul; when it appears, go to Settings > General > Software Update on your iPhone and tap install (per Apple's release notes at apple.com).

items.title: That 'Unpaid Ticket' Text Is a Scam — Delete It, Don't Tap It
items.summary: A wave of fake "DMV" text messages is hitting drivers across the country right now — texts claiming your license will be suspended for an unpaid ticket and demanding payment through a link. Florida's own DMV says it will NEVER text you demanding money or threatening suspension. If you tap the link, you hand your card to criminals. Delete the text, don't reply, and report it by forwarding to 7726.

items.title: Microsoft just sealed 974 security holes in one day — the update is free, here's how to confirm you got it
items.summary: Open Settings > Windows Update on your PC and click Check for updates — Microsoft released its biggest security update ever on September 9, covering 974 holes in Windows, including ones criminals were already using. It's free, it's built into Windows, and it takes about ten minutes.

items.title: Acer just made a laptop you can open like a car hood — the Vero 16 latches open with no tools
items.summary: Acer's new Vero 16 laptop has a latch on the bottom that pops open without a screwdriver, so its battery and storage are simple swaps anyone can do — see the full specs and a photo walkthrough at acer.com/us-en/laptops/vero/acer-vero-16.

items.title: A Shipping-Center Break-In Just Handed Scammers 81,000 Customer Lists
items.summary: A gadget-wallet maker called Trezor just revealed that a break-in at its shipping partner now touches 81,000 customers — names, home addresses, phone numbers, and order details, some from orders placed years ago. Lists like this are gold for scammers pretending to be real stores, so expect very convincing fake emails, calls, and letters. Don't trust a caller just because they know your name and what you bought — hang up and call the company back using the number on its real website.

items.title: Your laptop says it's full but your photos are already safe — OneDrive's "Free up space" clears the clutter without deleting anything
items.summary: If your laptop keeps saying "storage full," open your OneDrive folder, right-click the biggest folders (usually Pictures), and choose **"Free up space."** The photo stays safe in the cloud at onedrive.com — your laptop keeps a small shortcut instead of the full copy. OneDrive is built into Windows 10 and 11, no download needed.

items.title: Hate the giant Windows 11 Start menu? The latest free update lets you shrink it and move the taskbar — here's the setting
items.summary: Install the latest free update via **Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates**, then open **Settings > Personalization > Start** to shrink the menu and hide sections you never use, and **Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors** to move it where you want it.
